business_problem: Yichang Central People's Hospital needed a shared hospital-group data foundation that could standardize data definitions, improve governance, and support reporting, clinical alerts, and cross-department data services instead of spreadsheet-based and inconsistent reporting.
solution_summary: Yichang Central People's Hospital used a privately deployed medical data middle platform as the digital base for group-wide smart-hospital operations. The platform collects and standardizes clinical, operational, and management data so the hospital group can move toward "one system, one network, one hospital" governance. Standard management, model management, and master-data management align data definitions across institutions, while visual data-governance workflows reduce spreadsheet reporting errors and improve consistency with business systems. Tencent's platform also exposes API services to finance, logistics, HR, and discipline-construction centers, and supports partner-built applications through a CareDesign low-code layer and a pluggable DataPipeline engine. With shared operators for synchronization, quality control, EMPI, API calls, and transcoding, the hospital can power patient 360 views, reporting, clinical alerts, and BI from a common data asset base.

data_flow: Clinical, operational, and management data from hospital business systems is collected into the medical data middle platform, standardized through governance and master-data layers, processed through the DataPipeline engine, and then exposed as APIs, dashboards, alerts, and low-code applications.
business_outcome: The hospital gained a stronger governance and service foundation for smart-hospital operations, reducing reporting inconsistency while supporting shared data services, patient views, clinical alerts, and BI across the hospital group.
metrics: The platform includes more than 3,000 quality-control rules.
